newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Thursday due to the issue of domestic A shares by Tangshan Iron and Steel Co on the Shenzhen stock exchange, traders said.

The annual rate for the most active seven-day contract rose to 19.52 percent from 18.00 percent on Wednesday. Total turnover of the six-contract market surged to 13.2 million lots from 5.44 million on Wednesday.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Tangshan issued 120 million A shares at 9.22 yuan each, leading to a surge in demand on the repo market.
In addition, four other A firms will issue or list A shares on Friday on the Shenzhen and Shanghai bourses, boosting institutional borrowing, traders said.
"Securities houses were the biggest borrowers on the repo market today and they pushed up the rates," one trader said.
Traders said the rates were currently very high and were likely to move in a narrow range on Friday.

Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down in slow trading on Thursday, continuing a downward trend in the past couple of weeks with the bubbling A share markets making most investors leave the spot market, traders said.
The most active 10-year bond that matures in June 2006, a market barometer, fell to 115.96 yuan from 115.99 yuan.
Combined volume of the seven-contract market rose slightly to 1.09 million lots from 0.99 million lots.
"The spot market has been left out in the cold by securities investors due to the strong bull run on the A share markets," one trader said.

Traders said one indication of the sluggishness of the spot market was that few investors had bought the two contracts which stopped trading on Tuesday and Wednesday despite very high yields of more than 20 percent on maturity.
